blocks.x: He should read the score and know what instruments to bring up at the time.
And they don't make them like that no more.
Yeah, I haven't been interested in --
(Unintelligible) with Columbia Records, and Tio was there, he could read (inaudible).
Was that Plout, do you know, that --
Big guy, did a lot of classical dates, yeah.
Yeah, he was fantastic. But you say it's not the same now.

If you had the chance to -- if somebody gave you a grant, to make some records, and you'd be in charge of the whole operation in terms of picking the label, picking the studio, the A&R, the engineer, what would you do?
Tio-Becelle, I'd get Teddy Charles for
I'd get Tio Becelle for engineer, (inaudible) written music. I'd get Les Paul for the engineer.
I'd get some guy who knows electronic things. I'd try to get the guy who's in Columbia.
His last name, I think, is Plaut, P-l-a-u-t. I'm not sure that Fred is his first name.
And where would you do it?
Oh, on 30th Street or something like that.
With as much time as was needed, right?
Yeah. I don't know these studios (unintelligible), you know about those studios?
